new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Only one work is listed for this item and it was opened by the compiler, so there was no second silent/unopened work to spot-check within the list. As an extra check of the compiler relation_note I re-opened the on-disk Laycock 1965 (PL C-1) text and a full-text search for stress/accent chapter 12 'Outline grammar of the Ngala language' (the text layerprinted pp. 131-138) with a space-tolerant regex for stress/accent/tone/pitch/prominence: no hits; the book's only stress rules are the Wosera ones in 5.2 (pp. 29-30) and stress-conditioned allophony notes in the Manambu chapter, none applied to Ngala. So nothing on Ngala stress was missed in the works held by the project. No new works were ad…

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page ngal1300 and reference record 474375 (Aikhenvald 2015, 'Differential case in Yalaku', Oceanic Linguistics 54(1):240-269, tagged Yalaku [ylg])
sources.note: Bibliographic only: the languoid's refs are Laycock 1965 (pp.181,185-189, subclassification), Aikhenvald 2015 (about Yalaku, not Ngala) and Campbell et al. 2022 (endangerment); zero descriptive refs.

sources.citation: Foley, William A. 2005. Linguistic prehistory in the Sepik-Ramu basin. In Pawley, Attenborough, Golson & Hide (eds), Papuan Pasts, 109-144. Pacific Linguistics 572. (bitstream is the whole edited volume)
sources.note: Nothing on stress in Ndu; Ngala appears only in comparative pronoun/case tables; source list p.144 gives 'Ngala: Laycock (1965)' as the sole source.

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1991. Three vowels, semivowels, and neutralisation: orthographic and other problems of Sepik languages. In T. Dutton (ed.), Papers in Papuan linguistics 1, 107-114. Pacific Linguistics A-73.
sources.note: Ndu three-vowel system illustrated from Abelam; Ngala not mentioned; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1973. Sepik languages: checklist and preliminary classification. Pacific Linguistics B-25. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Listed in hh.bib for [nud]; a checklist/classification, very unlikely to state stress; open on the ANU repository (hdl 1885/146478) but not downloaded here.

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1965. The Ndu language family (Sepik District, New Guinea). Linguistic Circle of Canberra Publications / Pacific Linguistics C-1. Canberra: ANU. xi+224 pp. Ch. 12 'Outline grammar of the Ngala language', pp.131-138; sec. 12.2 'Phonology of Ngala' pp.131-133.
sources.note: Nothing for Ngala. 12.21-12.26 (pp.131-133, pp.143-145, page scan checked) cover phoneme inventory, allophony, complex nuclei, palatalisation and Wosera correspondences only; no mention of stress, accent, tone or length. The book's only stress rule is for Wosera Abelam (5.2, pp.29-30). pp.181-189 (Glottolog's cited pages) are lexicostatistics/family tree/Table XI structural comparisons with no stress row.

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1962. The Ndu language family (Sepik district, New Guinea). PhD thesis, Australian National University. 317 pp. Ch. 12 Ngala, typescript pp.178-186; 12.2 Phonology pp.179-181.
sources.note: Same content as the 1965 book for Ngala: phonemes, allophones, nuclei, correspondences; no stress statement. Stress is discussed only for Wosera (5.2), Boikin (9.31.4) and Manambu (11.31).
Stub; no phonology; cites only Ethnologue.
